summary: The first mismatch is the engraving location text on a grave at step 45. C read_engr_at asks dungeon.c:surface for that square and says headstone; JS read_engr_at hardcodes floor except ice despite having a source-backed dungeon.surface function. Correct that helper call and preserve the engraving message order. A later wand-object callback stop at step 49 is a separate zap.c:bhito behavior.

source.branch: read_engr_at sees nonempty HEADSTONE engraving text while the hero stands on a GRAVE; it obtains eloc from dungeon.c:surface(x,y), then prints the engraved-on-headstone message before the text.
callers: pickup.c:check_here/read_engr_at during hero movement onto a marked square
dependencies: dungeon.c:surface is already ported as js/dungeon.js:surface and returns headstone for IS_GRAVE
The later teleportation wand floor-object effect remains zap.c:bhito and is not part of this first mismatch

evidence: C engrave.c:318-359 obtains `const char *eloc = surface(x,y)` before the engraving-type switch; HEADSTONE and ENGRAVE print that eloc. C dungeon.c:1750-1788 returns `headstone` for IS_GRAVE after earlier terrain checks.

JS js/engrave.js:1251-1287 computes `surface = onIce ? ice : floor`, so its HEADSTONE arm says floor on a grave. JS js/dungeon.js:1772 already implements surface including the IS_GRAVE branch. This is a wrong helper choice in an existing implementation.

The v12 evaluation at challenges/evaluations/20260929033350-v12.json has 48/50 matched screens but its first differing glyph and cursor are at zero-based step 45, where C says headstone and JS says floor. The subsequent bhito(type 424) refusal at step 49 belongs to a different source branch and should remain visible after this repair.
The C-first manifest challenges/manifests/v12.json records the same first-mismatch attribution and independent C rerecording for this case.
